We present a computational framework for GRAG that enhances the generation capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by retrieving query-relevant textual subgraphs. To ensure efficient subgraph retrieval, we propose a divide-and-conquer strategy that leverages K-hop ego-graphs and soft pruning to approximate the optimal textual subgraph. Our approach provides LLMs with two complementary views of a textual graph: graph view and text view, enabling a comprehensive understanding of the graph context.
